title: Spending Time with the LORD
verse: The Lord would speak to Moses face to face, the way a person speaks to a friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his servant, Joshua son of Nun, a young man, did not leave the tent.
observation: Moses would separate himself from the people and meet with God. When he did, God would spend time with him as someone spends time with a friend. There is no indicator that God only wanted to do this with Moses. Because of Jesus, we can now walk with the LORD just like Moses. This is a great picture of what our devotional time with the LORD can be like. We find a place and time that is only for the LORD. It doesn’t matter how long it is. What matters is that it is for Him. Then, we speak with God as one speaks with a friend. The best part is we don’t have to leave God there. He continues to walk with us throughout the day.
application: Do you have a special time set aside where you spend one-on-one time with the LORD? This can be difficult due to your season of life or current living situation. Even if it is a time of silence among others, is there a set aside time you can give to the LORD? If so, do it and watch what starts to happen.
prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for desiring to have fellowship with us.
